questions.question: It was a very harmonious meeting without one ________ note.
The man was accused of committing a premeditated act, but he pleaded that it was ________.
We nearly lost the thread of his argument because of its complexity, but his language was our saving grace. The word opposite in meaning to "complexity" is ________.
Uche achieved ultimate success after overcoming many ________ difficulties.
I should know what to do in normal circumstances, but this is a very ________ situation.
Sola is quite extravagant whereas his wife is ________.
This is quite surprising; you cannot differentiate between the authentic and the ________ receipt.
Many people objected to the demolition of the tall gates whose ________ cost millions of dollars.
To some people, that culture is repugnant but to others it is ________.
While the armed robber remained unruffled after he had been arrested, his wife became ________.
Many people were seriously injured in the ________ accident; fortunately, nobody died.
The editor decided not to publish the ________ article since the writer did not indicate his name.
Dande did not fulfil the requirements for admission and so was ________ from taking the entrance examination.
The murder suspect denied the grave allegations against him, but the evidence so far has ________ him.
It was quite ________ to have invested in that new business.
The president granted the condemned prisoner a ________.
It was difficult for the doctor to ________ the patient's ailment.
They wished her ________ of the season.
Chief Koko never allows his name to be published in connection with his philanthropic activities because he ________ publicity.
A befitting ________ was paid to the memory of the departed renowned professor, playwright and dramatist.
The accused was caught red-handed by the police. This means that the accused was ________.
options: A. Made to wear red gloves
B. Thought to be in danger
C. Found in the very act

questions.question: The greatest problem of the leader is that he can see no further than his nose. This means that the leader ________.
He left the country to avoid loss of face. This means he left to ________.
options: A. Make his fortune somewhere else

questions.question: John was not really angry with Janet, but she seems to have taken the matter very much to heart. This means that Janet ________.
options: B. Is very upset about the matter
C. Has taken the matter very lightly
D. Has had a serious talk with him

questions.question: His driving made my hair stand on end. This means that his driving was ________.
When the riot broke out in the school, only the principal kept his head. This means that only the principal ________.
Grace failed Mathematics last year but she has promised to turn over a new leaf this year. This means that Grace will ________.
options: B. Work harder and change for the better
D. Examine both sides of a leaf

questions.question: The woman supported her husband through thick and thin. This means that she supported her husband ________.
options: A. In both good and bad health
B. When he was fat and when he became thin
C. Whether he behaved well or badly
D. In both good and bad circumstances

questions.question: Jumai thinks she is always right, but I am determined to catch her out. This means that I am determined to ________.
options: C. Prove that she can make a mistake
D. Make her agree that I am right

questions.question: The preacher advised those who lost their property in the fire disaster not to lose hope because every cloud has a silver lining. This means that ________.
options: A. There is a good side to every misfortune
B. When there is life there is hope
C. Loss is a common occurrence

questions.question: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "concede" as used in the sentence: "I concede that I am wrong on this point."
Within a short time, what was meant to be a peaceful demonstration escalated into a riot. The word "escalated" means ________.
The students were incensed to hear that their school fees had been substantially increased. The word "incensed" means ________.
The flood that swept away the entire village was a catastrophic event. The word "catastrophic" means ________.
The box contains the most valuable of all his possessions. The word "valuable" means ________.
The decision I have taken is irrevocable. The word "irrevocable" means ________.
I am delighted to speak before this august assembly. The word "august" means ________.
The chairman ended the meeting of the cooperative society with a fitting speech. The word "fitting" means ________.
The class was unusually disorderly today. The word "disorderly" means ________.
The report given by the boy is substantially correct and we have to decide what to do about it. The word "substantially" means ________.

essay.title: PAPER I - ESSAY, COMPREHENSION & SUMMARY
essay.instruction: SECTION A: Answer one (1) composition question. SECTION B and SECTION C are compulsory. Total theory score: 60 marks.

questions.question:
SECTION A — COMPOSITION (30 MARKS)
Your school recently organized an inter-house sports competition. Write a letter to a friend in another school describing the event and explaining what made it memorable.

Your essay should not be less than 400 words.

SECTION A — COMPOSITION (30 MARKS)
Write a letter to the chairman of your Local Government Area complaining about the poor condition of roads in your community and suggesting ways of improving the situation.

Your essay should not be less than 400 words.

SECTION A — COMPOSITION (30 MARKS)
Write an article for publication in a national newspaper on the dangers of examination malpractice among secondary school students.

Your essay should not be less than 400 words.

SECTION A — COMPOSITION (30 MARKS)
You are the chief speaker in a debate on the topic: "Social media has done more good than harm to secondary school students." Write your argument for or against the motion.

Your essay should not be less than 400 words.

SECTION A — COMPOSITION (30 MARKS)
Write a story that illustrates the saying: "A stitch in time saves nine."

Your essay should not be less than 400 words.

SECTION B — COMPREHENSION (15 MARKS)

Read the passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

For many years, residents of Oke-Ayo community had complained about the poor state of the only road connecting the village to the nearby town. During the dry season, clouds of dust covered houses and shops whenever vehicles passed. In the rainy season, the road became almost impossible to use because deep potholes filled with muddy water. Farmers often lost part of their produce because vehicles could not reach the farms in good time.

Several appeals had been made to the authorities, but little was done. Eventually, the community leaders decided that waiting endlessly for government intervention was no longer reasonable. They called a meeting at which every household agreed to contribute either money or labour towards repairing the worst portions of the road.

The response was impressive. Young people cleared the blocked drainage channels, while some adults supplied sand and stones. A few wealthy residents hired a tractor to grade the road. Although the work did not produce a perfect road, movement became considerably easier.

The project also produced an unexpected result. Residents who had previously shown little interest in community affairs began to cooperate more closely. They discovered that collective effort could solve some problems more quickly than constant complaints. Nevertheless, the village head reminded them that road construction remained primarily the responsibility of government and that the community's effort should not be used as an excuse for official neglect.

Answer the following questions:
(a) State two problems caused by the poor road during the rainy and dry seasons.
(b) Why did the community leaders decide to act on their own?
(c) Mention two contributions made by members of the community towards repairing the road.
(d) What unexpected benefit resulted from the road project?
(e) Why did the village head say the community's effort should not excuse government neglect?
(f) What does the expression "waiting endlessly" suggest about the attitude of the authorities?
(g) In the expression "who had previously shown little interest in community affairs":
(i) What is the grammatical name given to the expression?
(ii) What is its function?
(h) Give another word or phrase that can replace each of the following as used in the passage:
(i) intervention
(ii) impressive
(iii) considerably
(iv) collective
(v) neglect.

SECTION C — SUMMARY (15 MARKS)

Read the passage carefully and answer the question that follows.

Many students desire academic success, but not all of them are willing to adopt the habits that make success possible. Some wait until examinations are very close before they begin serious reading. Others spend long hours with their books but achieve little because they study without concentration or a clear plan.

Effective study begins with proper organization. A student should prepare a realistic timetable which gives adequate attention to every subject. Difficult subjects should not be avoided; rather, more time should be devoted to them. Regular revision also helps students to remember what they have learnt and reduces the pressure of last-minute preparation.

The environment in which a student studies is equally important. A quiet and well-lit place encourages concentration, while noise, mobile phones and unnecessary conversations can easily distract the learner. Students should also learn to take useful notes instead of attempting to memorize every sentence in a textbook.

Good health contributes greatly to effective learning. Adequate sleep, proper feeding and regular exercise help the mind to remain alert. A student who studies throughout the night without sufficient rest may discover that much of what was read is forgotten quickly.

Finally, successful students are willing to seek help when necessary. They ask teachers questions, discuss difficult topics with serious classmates and make use of relevant books and other educational materials. Academic excellence therefore depends not merely on intelligence but also on discipline, planning and consistent effort.

In five sentences, one for each point, summarize the habits that promote effective study and academic success.
